_description: Complete recipe for smoke effects in Niagara. Covers rising smoke, ground fog, dust cloud, and steam variants.

subuv_flipbook_material_recipe.when_to_use: Use this shared playbook when smoke is authored from a sprite sheet and Niagara playback is handled through ParticleSubUV.
subuv_flipbook_material_recipe.preferred_material_family: Translucent smoke material with ParticleSubUV, CameraDepthFade, and DepthFade. Prefer lit smoke for production quality; use unlit fallback only when sharing the same SubUV graph style as fire.
graph_summary: ParticleSubUV A -> Power with DynamicParameter.A -> * ParticleColor A -> * CameraDepthFade(DynamicParameter.B) -> DepthFade(DynamicParameter.G) -> Opacity
For lit smoke, drive BaseColor from ParticleSubUV RGB * ParticleColor RGB and keep emissive off or extremely low
For unlit fallback smoke, keep emissive restrained and let opacity silhouette stay the hero read
subuv_flipbook_material_recipe.authoring_rule: Do not treat smoke like additive fire. The fade silhouette must stay readable and broad, so DepthFade and low-emissive opacity shaping matter more than punch.

emitter_layers.name: Smoke_Main
emitter_layers.purpose: Primary visible smoke body — large, soft, billowing sprites
emitter_layers.material_notes: Lit smoke reacts to scene lighting → much more realistic than unlit. Use Volumetric NonDirectional for cheaper option.
emitter_layers.size_over_life: grow 2-4x over lifetime. Curve: slow start, accelerate in middle, plateau at end
emitter_layers.velocity: upward 50-200 cm/s + slight random horizontal ±30 cm/s
emitter_layers.opacity_note: Smoke should NEVER be fully opaque. Max 0.3-0.4 for thick smoke, 0.1-0.2 for light.

emitter_layers.name: Smoke_Detail
emitter_layers.purpose: Smaller, faster particles for surface detail and texture
emitter_layers.material_type: Same as main or different noise texture
emitter_layers.velocity: slightly faster than main, more horizontal variation
emitter_layers.opacity: lower than main (50-70% of main opacity)

emitter_layers.name: Wisps
emitter_layers.purpose: Thin trailing wisps at smoke edges
emitter_layers.initial_size: small start, grow large and very transparent
emitter_layers.velocity: slightly more horizontal than main, wind-influenced

modifications.color: smoke_light or smoke_dark depending on fuel

modifications.initial_velocity: higher (200-400 cm/s, driven by fire heat)
modifications.emissive: slight emissive at start (0.5-2.0) that fades quickly

modifications.velocity: mostly horizontal, very slow (10-30 cm/s), minimal upward
modifications.gravity: slight downward force to keep low
modifications.spawn_shape: large box or cylinder, wide and flat

dust_cloud.description: Kicked up dust from impact, footstep, or explosion

modifications.spawn_pattern: burst (10-30 particles) or short burst period

smoke_trail.description: Smoke trailing behind moving object (missile, vehicle)

modifications.drag: higher (0.4-0.6) so trail particles stop quickly
modifications.renderer: can use ribbon renderer for smooth trail

key_principles.never_fully_opaque: Real smoke is translucent. Max opacity 0.3-0.4 even for thick smoke.
key_principles.growth_is_essential: Smoke particles MUST grow over lifetime. Start small, end 2-4x larger.
key_principles.curl_noise_is_mandatory: Without curl noise, smoke looks like floating spheres. Always add curl noise force.
key_principles.variety_in_timing: Randomize lifetime ±20%, size ±30%, speed ±25% for natural look.
key_principles.lit_is_better: Use lit translucent material. Smoke that responds to light is dramatically more realistic.
key_principles.rotation_breaks_pattern: Random initial rotation + slow spin prevents obvious texture tiling.

niagara_modules_needed: Gravity Force (slight, optional — depends on variant)
Scale Color (color and opacity over life)
